The present application has been filed seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.

2. By way of appeal, the appellant seeks to assail the judgement of conviction dated 18.04.2024 vide which he has been convicted for offence punishable under Section 6 of POCSO Act and under Sections 363/366/376 (2) (f) (n) IPC as well as order on sentence dated 05.06.2024 vide which he has been directed to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 12 years for the offence punishable under Section 6 POCSO Act with fine of Rs.30,000/- and in default thereof to undergo SI for six months.
He was also sentenced to under RI for ten years under Section 366 IPC with fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default thereto to under SI for six months.
He was further This is a digitally signed order.

alongwith payment of fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default whereof, he was directed to further undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month.
The benefit of Section 428 Cr.P.C. has also been provided to the appellant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/applicant submits that in the trial, the prosecution has failed to conclusively prove the age of the victim, inasmuch as the age was proved through the school record obtained from the school which was not on the basis of municipal or government records or record from the first school of the victim.

He further submits that as per the victim's previous statement,
she had voluntarily gone with the appellant.
Thereafter, before recording of her deposition, she got married and consequently made a contradictory statement.
He further submits that the victim was more than 16 years of age and thus offence under Section 363 IPC is not made out as there is no enticement.

He submits that the hearing of the appeal would take some time and the appellant has already undergone sentence of 2 years 3 months and 26 days of sentence according to the nominal roll dated 30.07.2025 and he is not involved in any other case.

He further submits that the victim had attained the age of discretion and suggestions were given in the cross-examination on the aspect that she was more than 18 years of age at time of incident as her school records did not reflect her correct age.
4. The application is opposed by learned APP for the State duly assisted by learned counsel for the victim stating that the MLC as well as the FSL report supported the prosecution case.
5. Considering the contentions raised on the aspect of age would require detailed consideration.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 05/08/2025 at 22:26:55 considering the period already undergone by the appellant in custody, the sentence of the appellant/applicant is suspended during the pendency of the appeal on him furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court/ Duty J.M./ link J.M./Jail Superintendent and also subject to the further following conditions:-
(i) In case of change of residential address, the appellant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Investigating Officer as well as to this Court.
(ii) The appellant shall regularly appear before the Court as and when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
(iii) The appellant shall not, directly or indirectly get in touch with the prosecutrix.
6. With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
7. A copy of this order be communicated electronically forthwith to the concerned Jail Superintendent for information and necessary compliance.
8. Copy of this order be also uploaded on the website forthwith.
